# Experimental Apple decoder

Remora's explicit `apple` VNC mode implements one plaintext Apple RFB 003.889 profile. Standard mode remains the default. Apple mode requires security type 30 (ARD), an extended shared ServerInit without session selection, 32-bit RGB888 pixels, and an initial complete framebuffer baseline. It advertises only MVS encoding 1011 and Raw. Unsupported profiles and geometry changes end the attempt. There is no alternate authentication retry, whole-session encryption, virtual display, media, HEVC, clipboard synchronization or dynamic resizing.

`mvs.c` and `mvs.h` are the frozen v3 C port of [noVNC-ARD](https://github.com/peetinc/noVNC-ARD/tree/d699293635083c9e0c30c8f9480993865653772a/ard/decoders), revision `d699293635083c9e0c30c8f9480993865653772a`. The port covers full, partial, cache, match and quantization updates. The imported algorithm is unchanged. Only the historical scratch description and header guard were changed for this distribution. The originals had SHA-256 `7efd6151967b4bb1313f8f849cbd284663a5554542c8e459e144d0a470cd87fd` (C) and `2da0cf4349d12f2ed8289e399a230c011a7b609ed7299d3bec33f7c4e6f08c45` (header). The MPL-2.0 license is in `../licenses/Apple-MVS-MPL-2.0.txt`. The IDCT attribution and IJG notices are retained. New adapter code is GPL-3.0-or-later.

The reference JavaScript wraps IDCT intermediate arithmetic to 32 bits. This C port computes the transform in 64 bits with the documented 32-bit workspace. Independent valid-stream comparisons found differences when dequantized coefficient magnitudes reached 32768 or greater. Apple's behavior in that range is unverified. Partial-state accumulation prevents assuming that real content cannot reach it. No overflow emulation or decoder change is made here. Cache slots 1 through 64999 are supported and wrap to 1. Index 65000 always ends the session with a typed error, including cache-next after 64999. The JavaScript reference accepts this unwritten slot after 65000 inserts and reads past its typed array. Remora does not reproduce that behavior; Apple encoder/viewer behavior at that index is unknown. Full agreement with Apple's decoder, live display quality and real-host input usability remain unproven. The controlled Apple-viewer oracle covered only F0 and F1; its rejected F2 image was deleted and F3-F6 were not evaluated.

`apple.c` owns the private profile state. It parses bounded control bodies, limits compressed rectangles to the smaller of 64 MiB and `4 * rectangle area + 65536`, and accepts only aligned, framebuffer-contained MVS rectangles. The existing renderer limits remain 16384 pixels per axis and 67,108,864 pixels total. A malformed rectangle ends the session. There is no recovery using a partially consumed payload or a decoder that has failed.

Whole updates commit only after all rectangles validate. The adapter accumulates one bounding box from the decoder's existing written-tile callbacks and Raw rectangles, then publishes it once at the end of the message. DCT writes, cache loads and match copies contribute only their destination pixels, clipped at the framebuffer edge. Skipped tiles, skipped matches and quantization updates add no damage. A full MVS update publishes the entire desktop. The first complete baseline also publishes the entire desktop; unsupported geometry changes still end the attempt. One bounding box uses constant storage and preserves the existing single-rectangle renderer path. Distant writes can include unchanged pixels between them. No callback exposes an incomplete message, even if the decoder wrote pixels before detecting its error.

The adapter sends shared ClientInit `0x81` and control SetMode 1. After a complete baseline it enables full-region, zero-interval AutoFBUpdate (`0x09`). It sends no automatic type-3 request per pushed update. Hidden demand disables the subscription; resume enables it and preserves the existing immediate full-refresh request. Repeated demand does not generate refreshes. Closing the transport ends the subscription. Server messages ARDAck (`0x04`), NOP (`0x07`), StateChange (`0x14`) and DisplayInfo2 (`0x51`) are handled only in this profile. Basic and Apple pasteboard bodies are discarded in chunks of at most 4096 bytes, with a 1 MiB body limit. Unknown messages and unsupported rectangle encodings fail closed.

Individual key events use the source-defined type `0x10`, flag 0 and a 16-byte AES-128-ECB block. The block contains marker 255, direction, BE32 keysym, monotonic microseconds modulo 2^32 and six zero bytes. Only the ARD-derived 16-byte MD5 shared-secret key is retained after successful authentication. OpenSSL performs AES. Native state, key and block buffers are cleansed on failure, reinitialization and worker cleanup. No key enters Swift or diagnostics. This protects individual key-event formatting; the desktop transport remains unencrypted. The normal security selector still prefers VeNCrypt, but this Apple profile ends if the selected method is not ARD because no supported event key exists.

Option maps to Meta, legacy character keysyms above Latin-1 map to Unicode, and right/middle button bits swap at the Apple wire boundary. Source ownership stays in the existing input worker. Discrete scrolling follows ard-rs revision `7ff47199541c364cbba16e29c4410e39898ece0e`, `crates/ard-core/src/protocol.rs:917` and `crates/ard-viewer/src/session_runtime.rs:2058`. Positive native horizontal deltas correspond to RFB left (0x20); Remora right (0x40) becomes negative. Discrete scrolling uses the source-defined type `0x17`, subtype 11 record with line, 16.16 and point deltas, the event position, and the existing held-button mask. A local system arrow is explicitly emitted; unsupported remote cursor-shape encodings are not advertised.

`../patches/libvncclient-apple.patch` connects this module to the pinned LibVNCClient without changing standard-mode parsing or authentication selection. `../build-vnc.sh` compiles this decoder in the Release engine with `-O3`, using the existing OpenSSL archive. `../tests/test-apple-mvs.sh` runs the owned vectors and bounded fuzz cases under ASan/UBSan. `python3 Vendor/tests/test-apple-session.py` drives the sanitized adapter and decoder through the public native API with an independently authenticated loopback peer. Swift public-session tests exercise the same wire framing and independent CommonCrypto key-event decryption. None of these tests establish Apple-viewer fidelity or real-host usability.

## Responsiveness on LAN

On 2026-11-08 Remora 038966d was measured against macOS Screen Sharing (Adaptive Quality) on the same macOS 27 MacBook Pro over wired LAN (0.9 ms ping). A local probe posted a real input event, captured the client window with ScreenCaptureKit at 120 frames per second, and timed the first frame in which the watched region changed. The actions were scrolling TextEdit by six lines, typing Return and Delete in TextEdit, and opening and closing a menu. Each cell is the median of the per-round medians, with 10 to 16 trials per action per round. Remora Apple mode and Screen Sharing ran one at a time in alternating rounds, so each pair saw the same remote conditions. Standard mode ran once on the same build.

| Client | Scroll | Return/Delete | Menu | Rounds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Remora Apple mode | 92 ms | 103 ms | 121 ms | 6 (menu: 3) |
| macOS Screen Sharing | 72 ms | 82 ms | 91 ms | 6 (menu: 3) |
| Remora standard mode | 93 ms, slowest 10% over 614 ms | 771 ms | 107 ms, slowest 25% over 1105 ms | 1 |

Remote conditions moved both clients between 58 ms and 135 ms medians within an hour. Remora's best rounds matched Screen Sharing (scroll 65.7 ms against 69.2 ms), and some rounds were 20 to 90 ms slower. Before this work the same probe measured Apple mode at 97, 104 and 128 ms and standard mode at 653, 863 and 758 ms.

Signposts split each response into stages. Remora's own share is about 15 ms: input reaches the wire in about 1.5 ms, ingest and presentation take about 3 ms, and the compositor takes about 10 ms. The rest is the remote Mac. From our input reaching the wire to the first changed update arriving takes 63 to 87 ms median. That update is about 4 KB in one rectangle and is read in 0.3 ms. At idle the server pushes about 45 full-desktop MVS updates per second of 45 to 85 bytes each. Sending an incremental FramebufferUpdateRequest after each input batch, which the server serves before its automatic-update pacing, made no measurable difference in an alternating A/B test, so it is not included.

A 344-second editing session in Apple mode, with typing, scrolling and menus, produced no decoding errors. Its framebuffer matched a fresh full update at 52.9 dB; the only differing tiles held the menu bar clock. Pressing Escape in Preview's empty search field leaves the field's focus ring visible in both Remora and Screen Sharing, so that behavior comes from Preview.
